subject: Urgent: Zenith production throughput collapse — remediation & commercial proposal
messages:
From: Michael Turner <michael.turner@zenith.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: severe throughput collapse affecting batch jobs

Diego,

We're seeing a dramatic throughput collapse on our production workload beginning around 08:40 PDT this morning. Batch inference latency spiked from ~150ms/token to >1.2s/token and a large swath of requests started returning 5xx errors. This has blocked several downstream pipelines and caused material downstream delays for customer-facing features.

Attached are sampled error logs and a short list of impacted jobs. At a minimum we need: 
- Immediate confirmation of root cause and expected ETA to restore baseline throughput
- A commercial remediation plan if this is an SLA breach
- A point of contact for exec escalation (CC'ing Lisa Han and procurement).

We are on a tight rollout window and can't afford extended instability. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Michael Turner
Head of Platform
Zenith AI

Date: 2027-05-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: severe throughput collapse affecting batch jobs

Michael — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're investigating as high priority.

On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 9:12 AM Michael Turner <michael.turner@zenith.ai> wrote:
> Diego,
>
> We're seeing a dramatic throughput collapse ...

Immediate actions from our side:
- I've looped in Rishi (serving runtime lead) and Marissa (CS lead) to coordinate between engineering and your account team.
- We've opened an incident and started a trace across the serving fleet; initial signs point to a regression in the batching heuristic when request concurrency exceeds a short threshold (we're validating).
- I'll provide an internal timeline within 90 minutes and an interim mitigation if we can reproduce in a staging bucket.

For transparency: if this meets our SLA breach thresholds (errors/latency windows), we will prepare a remediation credit proposal and a short-term operational mitigation (e.g., temporary routing to a reserve pool). I will not speculate on amounts until we have precise impact metrics.

Point of contact: me (diego_fernandez@redwood.ai) and Rishi (rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai). We'll keep Lisa and procurement updated.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Production: severe throughput collapse affecting batch jobs — preliminary findings

Diego / Marissa,

Preliminary technical findings:
- Root cause: a change in the continuous batching threshold selector combined with a sequence-length distribution shift in Zenith's workload produced suboptimal batching decisions. This created oversized KV cache churn and request head-of-line blocking under sustained concurrency.
- Impact window: 2027-05-02T08:38–2027-05-02T10:25 PDT.
- Measured impact for the largest job group: median per-token latency rose from 150ms -> 1.1s, error rate increased from 0.2% -> 6.8%.

Mitigations already attempted:
1) Forced fallback to conservative batching profile for Zenith traffic (immediate, reduced error rate but higher per-request compute cost).
2) Evicted some KV cache partitions and applied a hot-key routing rule to spread load (reduced queuing).

Status: baseline throughput recovered to within 15% of prior medians as of 2027-05-03T07:10 PDT, but the traffic pattern still shows elevated variance on certain job classes. We will:
- Ship a patch that adjusts the selector logic and adds an emergency routing bypass for batch windows (ETA 12 hours).
- Produce precise token-level impact numbers for the billing window (will attach the chart).

I've attached a throughput chart and a short incident timeline.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Internal: Zenith outage — proposed commercial remediation and next steps

Evelyn / Marissa —

Summary: Rishi confirmed a platform regression that materially impacted Zenith between 05/02 08:38–10:25 PDT. Zenith is rightly asking for both technical remediation and commercial redress. They are a strategic mid-market account (annualized run rate ~ $680k) and procurement is involved.

Proposed commercial remediation (initial offer):
- One-time credit equal to 15% of May bill (applies to the billing period containing the incident).
- 200 dedicated GPU-hours (Reserved pool credit) to use within 60 days for capacity isolation testing or burst windows.
- Commitment to a post-incident technical review within 7 business days and a bi-weekly follow-up for the next 6 weeks.

Rationale: This mixes an immediate monetary remedy (visible in billing) with operational credits that help prevent recurrence and reduce Zenith's near-term risk. The 15% figure is aligned with our historical compensation band for a ~2-hour full-service degradation impacting heavy job classes.

Attachments: zenith_sla_draft_credit_0504.pdf (one-page credit memo + DocuSign redirect).

If approved, I'll send a customer-facing note with the numbers and the DocuSign link. If you want to escalate higher or change numbers (e.g., 20% or additional month-of-credit), let me know — I want to get Marissa and procurement the draft today.

— Diego
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Michael — thanks again for patience while we dug in.

On behalf of Redwood, here is our remediation package for the 2027-05-02 incident: 
- One-time credit equal to 15% of Zenith's May 2027 invoice, applied as an account credit within 7 business days of signature.
- 200 GPU-hours of Dedicated pool credit to use within 60 days (can be used for isolated test runs or burst capacity).
- A full technical RCA and a joint post-incident review scheduled for the week of May 10; bi-weekly checkpoints for 6 weeks thereafter.

You can review and sign the credit memo here: https://docusign.com/ZN-4821-credit-agreement

If this package doesn't meet Zenith's needs, tell me the shortfall (e.g., % credit or additional SLA wording) and we'll escalate internally. We value the relationship and want to close this together.
